chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abdul Malik ibn Ayn, who said:

A group of our companions performed Hajj. So when they arrived in Medina, they visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'Zurara instructed us to begin with the Hajj (by saying 'Labbayk Hajj') when we enter the state of Ihram.' So he (peace be upon him) said to them, 'Perform Tamattu'.' So when they left his presence, I entered upon him and said, 'May I be your ransom! If you do not inform them with what you informed Zurara, we will go to Kufa and they will consider him a liar.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Bring them back.' So they entered upon him, and he (peace be upon him) said, 'Zurara spoke the truth.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, no one will hear this from me after this day.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْكُوفَة: Kufa, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.تَمَتَّعُوا: Perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams
key_terms.نُهِلَّ: We begin by saying 'Labbayk' (Here I am) with a specific intention

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say about Zurara's instruction regarding the type of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *al-tawassu'* (flexibility) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam (peace be upon him) validates Zurara’s specific instruction for Hajj al-Qiran while also permitting Tamattu', demonstrating that multiple valid modes of Ihram can coexist without contradiction. The Imam’s final declaration that 'no one will hear this from me after today' highlights the transition from specific contextual rulings to general principles, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the stability of legal rulings. It underscores the reliability of Zurara as a primary narrator and the Imam’s authority to confirm or modify practices based on the companions' understanding.
